title: Vanishing of the raw truncation couple in the lower half plane
statement: theorem truncation_quadrant_vanishing {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₁} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} A] {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₂} B] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} B] (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] (K : CochainComplex.Plus A) (a : ℤ) (ha : ∀ q : ℤ, q < a → IsZero (K.obj.homology q)) : (∀ p q : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero (TruncationCouple.E F K p q)) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, q < a → IsZero (TruncationCouple.D F K p q)) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, q < a → IsZero (TruncationCouple.E F K p q))

source.place: proof, step 3; Lean refinement with the same objects and canonical maps

proof.text:
For q<a the truncation has zero homology in every degree: below and at q
use the homology isomorphism of its inclusion and the hypothesis on K; above q
use strict upper support. Its image in the derived category is zero, and additive
RF and homology preserve zero objects. For E with q<a the single complex is zero
because H^q(K) is zero. For p<0, RF of the degree-zero single object has no negative
homology; shift it by -q and use commutation of RF and homology with shifts.
Finally transport all three zero-object assertions through `bridgeIso`. The negative-degree assertion uses Functor.isGE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj_singleFunctor from src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility directly; zero objects are detected by DerivedCategory.isZero_of_forall_isZero_homology from the proved source library.
